q: A railway servant applies for a Motor Car Advance for purchasing a car for his personal use. Under the 7th CPC dispensation, his application cannot be entertained because:

options.A: Among the interest-bearing advances, only House Building Advance and Personal Computer Advance continue to be admissible, and the Motor Car Advance stands discontinued
options.B: Motor Car Advance is admissible only to gazetted officers
options.C: Motor Car Advance is admissible only after completion of 20 years of service
options.D: The advance has merely been renamed and is payable without interest

e: Under the 7th CPC, most interest-bearing advances were abolished; only House Building Advance and Personal Computer Advance continue, so Motor Car Advance is no longer admissible.

q: The house of a railway servant is affected by a severe flood and he applies for a Flood Advance. The position regarding Flood Advance under the 7th CPC dispensation is:

options.D: The advance stands abolished and is no longer admissible

e: Flood Advance was among the interest-free advances abolished on the 7th CPC recommendations, so it is no longer admissible to railway servants.

q: Under the Unique Medical Identity (UMID) initiative on the Railways, a railway servant or his dependent can avail treatment at any railway hospital or health unit by producing:

options.A: Only the medical identity card issued by his own unit, valid nowhere else
options.B: A fresh referral letter from his controlling officer on every occasion
options.C: The UMID smart card, which serves as a uniform medical identity across railway health units
options.D: His privilege pass, which doubles as a medical identity card

e: UMID provides a uniform smart card identity, so the holder can get treatment at any railway hospital or health unit, not only the issuing unit.

q: An applicant under the Right to Information Act, 2005, whose first appeal has been disposed of by the First Appellate Authority, may prefer a second appeal to the Central Information Commission within a period of:

options.A: 30 days from the date of the decision of the First Appellate Authority
options.B: 90 days from the date on which the decision of the First Appellate Authority should have been made or was actually received
options.C: One year from the date of the original application
options.D: 15 days from the date of the decision of the First Appellate Authority

e: Section 19 of the RTI Act, 2005 allows a second appeal to the Central Information Commission within 90 days from the date the First Appellate Authority decision should have been made or was received.

q: An application for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005, made to a Central Public Information Officer of the Railways, is ordinarily required to be accompanied by an application fee of:

options.A: Rs 10
options.B: Rs 50
options.C: Rs 100
options.D: Rs 500

e: The RTI (Fee and Cost) Rules prescribe an application fee of Rs 10 for information sought from a Central Public Information Officer.

q: An official act of a railway servant, done in good faith in the discharge of his duties, is criticised adversely. Under Rule 11 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in order to vindicate that official act, the railway servant:

options.A: May freely approach the press for publication of his version
options.B: May file a court case without informing the Government
options.C: May issue a public statement on his own authority
options.D: Shall not, except with the previous sanction of the Government, have recourse to any court or to the press for the vindication of the official act

e: Rule 11 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 bars a railway servant from having recourse to any court or the press to vindicate an official act except with previous Government sanction.

q: A disciplinary authority proposes to punish a railway servant by withholding one increment of his pay for a period of one year, without cumulative effect, that is, without postponing his future increments. This penalty is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as:

options.A: A major penalty
options.B: Not a penalty at all
options.C: A minor penalty
options.D: A penalty only if imposed on a gazetted railway servant

e: Withholding of increments without cumulative effect is listed as a minor penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, unlike withholding with cumulative effect, which is major.

q: A railway servant had validly nominated his wife to receive the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity payable on his death, and had also named an alternate nominee in the same nomination. His wife dies during his lifetime, before his retirement. The effect of her death on the nomination is that:

options.A: The entire gratuity becomes payable to the Government on his death
options.B: The nomination becomes invalid to the extent it relates to his wife, and the share is payable to the alternate nominee named in the nomination
options.C: The nomination in favour of his wife continues to operate in favour of her legal heirs automatically
options.D: He is debarred from making any fresh nomination during his service

e: On the death of a nominee for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity, the nomination becomes invalid to that extent, and the share becomes payable to the alternate nominee named, if any.

q: In regard to the maintenance of the Service Book of a non-gazetted railway servant, the prescribed practice for verification of its entries is that:

options.A: The Service Book is shown to the railway servant every year and his signature is obtained in token of having verified the entries
options.B: The Service Book is never shown to the railway servant during his service
options.C: The railway servant verifies his Service Book only once, at the time of his retirement
options.D: Verification of the Service Book is done only by the Accounts Office, without the knowledge of the railway servant

e: The Service Book of a non-gazetted servant is to be shown to him every year and his signature obtained in token of verification of the entries therein.

q: Personnel of the Railway Protection Force, who are not covered by the Productivity Linked Bonus scheme applicable to other railway employees, are granted an ad-hoc bonus equivalent to:

options.A: 78 days' emoluments, on the same lines as the Productivity Linked Bonus
options.B: 15 days' emoluments
options.C: 60 days' emoluments
options.D: 30 days' emoluments

e: RPF personnel, excluded from Productivity Linked Bonus, are paid an ad-hoc bonus equivalent to 30 days emoluments.

q: A female railway servant applies for Child Care Leave for the care of her third child, her two elder surviving children being grown up and no longer in her care. Her application is liable to be rejected because:

options.A: Child Care Leave is admissible only in respect of the first child of the employee
options.B: Child Care Leave can be granted only by the Railway Board in such cases
options.C: Child Care Leave is admissible only in respect of the two eldest surviving children of the employee
options.D: Child Care Leave is admissible for any number of children without restriction

e: Child Care Leave is admissible only for the two eldest surviving children, so it cannot be granted for a third child even if the elder children are grown up.

q: In regard to the leave account of a male railway servant who is granted paternity leave, the correct position is that:

options.A: Paternity leave is debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: Paternity leave is not debited to his leave account
options.C: Paternity leave is debited to his Leave on Half Average Pay account
options.D: Twice the number of days of paternity leave is debited to his leave account

e: Paternity leave is a separate leave facility and is not debited to the Leave on Average Pay or any other leave account of the male railway servant.

q: A railway servant is appointed to railway service on 1st October. Leave on Average Pay is credited in advance in instalments of 15 days on 1st January and 1st July, at the rate of two and a half days for each completed month of service. The Leave on Average Pay to be credited to his account for the broken period of his first half-year of service, covering the three months from October to December, is:

options.A: 7.5 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 2.5 days

e: Leave on Average Pay accrues at 2.5 days per completed month; for October to December, 3 months x 2.5 days = 7.5 days.

q: The widow of a deceased railway servant is in receipt of family pension of Rs 30,000 per month. On her attaining the age of 85 years, the additional quantum of family pension admissible to her, at 30 per cent of her family pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 6,000 per month
options.B: Rs 15,000 per month
options.C: No additional quantum is admissible on family pension
options.D: Rs 9,000 per month

e: Additional family pension at age 85 is 30 per cent of family pension; 30 per cent of Rs 30,000 = Rs 9,000 per month.

q: An ex-serviceman who had rendered 12 years of service in the armed forces is considered for appointment to a civil post on the Railways against a vacancy reserved for ex-servicemen. For the purpose of the upper age limit for the post, the relaxation admissible to him is worked out by deducting from his actual age:

options.A: Only the period of his military service, without any addition
options.B: A flat period of five years in all cases
options.C: The period of his military service plus three years
options.D: The period of his military service plus ten years

e: For ex-servicemen, upper age relaxation is by deducting the period of military service plus three years from the actual age; here the formula, not a flat five years, applies.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 33 years of qualifying service, that is, 66 completed six-monthly periods. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 1,40,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him will be:

options.A: Rs 23,10,000, being one-fourth of his emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service
options.B: Rs 16,50,000, being 16 and a half times his emoluments
options.C: Rs 25,00,000, the amount worked out at one-fourth of emoluments for each six-monthly period being restricted to the prescribed ceiling
options.D: Rs 11,55,000, being half a month's emoluments for each completed year of qualifying service

e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period: Rs 1,40,000 / 4 x 66 = Rs 23,10,000, which is also 16.5 times emoluments and below the ceiling.

q: A railway servant on sanctioned leave is compulsorily recalled to duty by the competent authority before the expiry of his leave, in the exigencies of service. In regard to his recall, he is entitled to:

options.A: Payment of double leave salary for the unexpired portion of his leave
options.B: Travelling allowance for the journey undertaken by him to rejoin duty on recall
options.C: A fresh spell of leave equal to twice the unexpired portion of the leave
options.D: No facility of any kind, the recall being purely an administrative action

e: A servant compulsorily recalled from sanctioned leave in the exigencies of service is entitled to Travelling Allowance for the journey to rejoin duty on recall.

q: A railway servant is granted Special Disability Leave for a period extending beyond 120 days for a disability arising out of an injury sustained in the discharge of his duty. The leave salary admissible to him during this leave is:

options.A: Equal to the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay for the first 120 days, and equal to that admissible on Leave on Half Average Pay for the remaining period
options.B: Half of the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay throughout the period of the leave
options.C: Equal to the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay throughout the period of the leave, without any limit
options.D: Nil for the period beyond 120 days, as no leave salary is admissible thereafter

e: Special Disability Leave salary equals Leave on Average Pay salary for the first 120 days and Leave on Half Average Pay salary for the remaining period.

q: A female railway servant has already availed Child Care Leave in three spells during the current calendar year and applies for a fourth spell in the same year for the care of her eldest surviving child. Her application is liable to be:

options.A: Granted, as there is no limit on the number of spells in a year
options.B: Granted, provided each spell is of not less than 15 days
options.C: Granted, if the leave is combined with Leave on Average Pay
options.D: Refused, as Child Care Leave cannot be granted in more than three spells in a calendar year

e: Child Care Leave cannot be granted in more than three spells in a calendar year, so a fourth spell in the same year must be refused.

q: A female railway servant, having less than two surviving children, legally adopts a child who is eight months old and applies for Child Adoption Leave. The leave admissible to her is:

options.A: 90 days from the date the child is handed over to her
options.B: 180 days from the date the child is handed over to her
options.C: 135 days from the date of the adoption deed
options.D: 60 days from the date the child is handed over to her

e: A female servant with less than two surviving children adopting a child below one year of age gets Child Adoption Leave of 180 days from the date the child is handed over.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing eight months of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 52,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family will be:

options.A: Rs 1,04,000, being two times his emoluments
options.B: Rs 3,12,000, being six times his emoluments
options.C: Rs 6,24,000, being twelve times his emoluments
options.D: Rs 26,000, being half a month's emoluments

e: Death gratuity for service of less than one year is two times emoluments; 2 x Rs 52,000 = Rs 1,04,000.

q: A railway servant gives three months' notice seeking voluntary retirement from service. The appointing authority does not refuse permission for his retirement before the expiry of the notice period. The correct position is that:

options.A: The notice lapses and the railway servant must continue in service
options.B: The railway servant must obtain a fresh written order permitting his retirement
options.C: The retirement takes effect automatically on the expiry of the notice period
options.D: The notice period stands extended by a further three months by default

e: Under the voluntary retirement rules, if the appointing authority does not refuse permission before the notice expires, retirement takes effect automatically on expiry of the notice.

q: A railway servant discovers, six years after entering service, that his date of birth has been recorded wrongly in his service records owing to a bona fide clerical error, and requests its alteration. His request is liable to be:

options.A: Entertained, as clerical errors can be corrected at any time during service
options.B: Refused, as a request for alteration of date of birth can be entertained only if made within five years of entering service
options.C: Entertained only if he produces a decree of a civil court
options.D: Refused, as the date of birth once recorded can never be altered in any circumstance

e: Alteration of date of birth can be entertained only if the request is made within five years of entering service, even where a bona fide clerical error is claimed.

q: A railway servant frequently purchases and sells shares and securities through a broker, several times every month, in the hope of quick gains. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, his activity is treated as:

options.A: A permissible investment, as it is made through a recognised stock broker
options.B: A permissible activity, as occasional investment in shares is allowed
options.C: A permissible activity, provided he intimates each transaction to his office
options.D: Speculation in investments, which is prohibited for a railway servant

e: Frequent purchase and sale of shares for quick gains is speculation, which the Conduct Rules prohibit; only occasional investment through a recognised broker is permitted.

q: A railway servant becomes a member of a political party while continuing in service, though he does not hold any office in the party and takes no part in its activities. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, his conduct is:

options.A: Impermissible, as a railway servant shall not be a member of, or otherwise associated with, any political party or organisation which takes part in politics
options.B: Permissible, as mere membership without holding office is not barred
options.C: Permissible, as the bar applies only to contesting elections
options.D: Permissible, provided he obtains the prior permission of his controlling officer

e: Rule 18 of the Conduct Rules provides that no railway servant shall be a member of or otherwise associated with any political party or organisation taking part in politics.

q: A railway servant proposes to own, in part, and participate in the management of a periodical publication brought out by a private publisher. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, he can do so only:

options.A: If the publication is of a purely literary character
options.B: If he does not draw any remuneration from the publication
options.C: With the previous sanction of the competent authority
options.D: If he carries on the activity entirely outside his office hours

e: Owning or managing a periodical publication requires the previous sanction of the competent authority under the Conduct Rules on private work and publications.

q: A railway servant is arrested on a criminal charge and is released on bail the next day. Apart from any question of suspension, the conduct expected of him under the rules is that he shall:

options.A: Keep the matter entirely to himself, as the case is sub judice
options.B: Report the fact of his arrest, and the circumstances connected with it, to his official superior as soon as possible
options.C: Report the matter only if he is eventually convicted by the court
options.D: Apply for casual leave for the period of his custody and say nothing further

e: A railway servant arrested on a criminal charge must report the fact of arrest and the circumstances to his official superior as soon as possible.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 70,000 per month is posted in a city classified as 'X' for the purpose of House Rent Allowance. Dearness Allowance payable to railway servants has crossed 50 per cent. The House Rent Allowance admissible to him per month will be:

options.A: Rs 16,800, at the rate of 24 per cent of his basic pay
options.B: Rs 18,900, at the rate of 27 per cent of his basic pay
options.C: Rs 12,600, at the rate of 18 per cent of his basic pay
options.D: Rs 21,000, at the rate of 30 per cent of his basic pay

e: When Dearness Allowance crosses 50 per cent, House Rent Allowance for X class cities rises to 30 per cent of basic pay; 30 per cent of Rs 70,000 = Rs 21,000.

q: A complaint of sexual harassment against a railway servant is inquired into by the Internal Complaints Committee constituted under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013. In the disciplinary proceedings against the railway servant, the report of the Committee is treated as:

options.A: A report of inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, on the basis of which the disciplinary authority may proceed
options.B: A mere preliminary fact-finding note having no bearing on the disciplinary proceedings
options.C: A final order of punishment which the disciplinary authority must implement without modification
options.D: Evidence which can be used only if a separate departmental inquiry reaches the same conclusion

e: Under the POSH Act framework as applied in the D and A Rules, the Internal Complaints Committee report is treated as an inquiry report for disciplinary proceedings.

q: A Central Public Information Officer of the Railways, without any reasonable cause, malafidely refuses to receive an application for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The penalty that may be imposed on him by the Central Information Commission is:

options.A: Rs 100 for each day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs 10,000
options.B: Rs 500 for each day of default, without any maximum ceiling
options.C: Rs 250 for each day till the application is received or the information is furnished, subject to a maximum of Rs 25,000
options.D: A flat penalty of Rs 50,000, irrespective of the period of default

e: Section 20 of the RTI Act prescribes penalty of Rs 250 per day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs 25,000, for malafide refusal or delay by the CPIO.

q: An adult worker employed in a railway workshop, governed by the Factories Act, 1948, has worked for 240 days or more in a calendar year. In the subsequent year, he is entitled to leave with wages at the rate of:

options.A: One day for every 15 days of work performed by him
options.B: One day for every 20 days of work performed by him
options.C: One day for every 25 days of work performed by him
options.D: One day for every 10 days of work performed by him

e: Section 79 of the Factories Act, 1948 gives an adult worker who worked 240 days or more leave with wages at one day for every 20 days of work performed.

q: A casual labourer on the Railways, who had been granted temporary status, is absorbed in a regular post. For the purpose of pension, the period of service rendered by him while in temporary status is counted as qualifying service to the extent of:

options.A: 25 per cent of that period
options.B: 100 per cent of that period
options.C: 75 per cent of that period
options.D: 50 per cent of that period

e: On absorption after temporary status, only 50 per cent of the casual labour service rendered with temporary status counts as qualifying service for pension.

q: In a railway accounts office, a question arises as to the record in which sanctions for the creation, extension and continuance of posts in the office are entered and watched. That record is the:

options.A: Book of Sanctions
options.B: Scale check register
options.C: Cadre register of the division
options.D: Register of penalties imposed on staff

e: The Book of Sanctions is the record in which sanctions for creation, extension and continuance of posts are entered and watched in an office.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation while in occupation of a railway quarter, which he vacates on retirement. His last basic pay is Rs 90,000 per month. The Composite Transfer Grant admissible to him on retirement will be:

options.A: Rs 90,000, being 100 per cent of his last basic pay
options.B: Rs 45,000, being 50 per cent of his last basic pay
options.C: Rs 72,000, being 80 per cent of his last basic pay
options.D: Rs 29,700, being 33 per cent of his last basic pay

e: Composite Transfer Grant on retirement is admissible at 80 per cent of last basic pay; 80 per cent of Rs 90,000 = Rs 72,000.

q: It is detected that a railway servant was paid pay at a higher rate than admissible for a continuous period of more than five years, entirely due to a mistake of the office, and a recovery of the excess payment is ordered just before his retirement. In accordance with the settled principles governing recovery of excess payments from employees, such recovery is:

options.A: Impermissible, as the excess payment was made for a period in excess of five years before the order of recovery
options.B: Permissible in full, as Government money wrongly paid must always be recovered
options.C: Permissible to the extent of one-half of the excess amount
options.D: Permissible only from his gratuity, and not from his pay or pension

e: As per the Rafiq Masih principles adopted by Government, recovery is impermissible where excess payment was made for a period in excess of five years before the recovery order, through no fault of the employee.

q: The retirement gratuity of a railway servant is not paid to him for over a year after his retirement, the delay being attributable to administrative lapse in his office and no departmental or judicial proceedings being pending against him. In such a case, he is entitled to:

options.A: No interest, as gratuity does not carry interest in any circumstance
options.B: Interest only if he obtains a decree from a court of law
options.C: Interest at the rate of 18 per cent per annum for the entire period of delay
options.D: Interest on the gratuity for the period of delay, at the rate applicable to General Provident Fund accumulations

e: Delayed payment of gratuity due to administrative lapse carries interest for the period of delay at the rate applicable to General Provident Fund accumulations.

q: A railway medical officer, who is debarred from private practice, claims Non-Practising Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation. The allowance is payable to him at the rate of:

options.A: 20 per cent of his basic pay
options.B: 25 per cent of his basic pay
options.C: 15 per cent of his basic pay
options.D: 30 per cent of his basic pay

e: Non-Practising Allowance for medical officers debarred from private practice is payable at 20 per cent of basic pay under the 7th CPC.

q: A senior instructor posted in a railway training institution, other than a national academy, claims Training Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation. The allowance admissible to him is:

options.A: 24 per cent of his basic pay
options.B: 10 per cent of his basic pay
options.C: 12 per cent of his basic pay
options.D: 30 per cent of his basic pay

e: Training Allowance for instructors in training institutions other than national academies is 12 per cent of basic pay under the 7th CPC; the 24 per cent rate is for national academies.

q: A railway servant entitled to Dress Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation enquires when the allowance for a year is credited to him. The correct position is that it is paid:

options.A: Every month along with his salary
options.B: Once in a year, in the month of July
options.C: Once in two years, in the month of January
options.D: Only once, at the time of his initial appointment

e: Dress Allowance is credited once a year in the month of July to eligible railway servants under the 7th CPC dispensation.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 60,000 per month is sent on deputation to an ex-cadre post at another station, the deputation involving a change of station. The Deputation (Duty) Allowance admissible to him per month will be:

options.A: Rs 3,000, being 5 per cent of his basic pay
options.B: Rs 9,000, being 15 per cent of his basic pay
options.C: Rs 1,500, being 2.5 per cent of his basic pay
options.D: Rs 6,000, being 10 per cent of his basic pay

e: Deputation (Duty) Allowance involving change of station is 10 per cent of basic pay, subject to the ceiling; 10 per cent of Rs 60,000 = Rs 6,000, within the ceiling.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 18 years of qualifying service and claims post-retirement complimentary passes. His claim is liable to be:

options.A: Rejected, as post-retirement complimentary passes are admissible only on rendering a minimum qualifying service of 20 years
options.B: Accepted, as the minimum qualifying service required is 10 years
options.C: Accepted, as the minimum qualifying service required is 15 years
options.D: Accepted in part, at half the normal number of sets

e: Post-retirement complimentary passes require a minimum qualifying service of 20 years, so a servant with only 18 years is not eligible.

q: A railway servant undertakes a journey with his family on a Privilege Ticket Order (PTO) issued to him. The fare payable by him for the journey is:

options.A: Half of the public fare for the class of travel
options.B: 25 per cent of the public fare for the class of travel
options.C: One-third of the public fare for the class of travel
options.D: Nil, as a PTO is equivalent to a free privilege pass

e: On a Privilege Ticket Order the railway servant pays one-third of the public fare for the class of travel, unlike a privilege pass which is free.

q: A penalty is imposed on a gazetted railway servant by an order passed by the President of India. In regard to an appeal against that order under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the correct position is that:

options.A: An appeal lies to the Railway Board
options.B: No appeal lies against an order passed by the President
options.C: An appeal lies to the Union Public Service Commission
options.D: An appeal lies to the Central Administrative Tribunal as an appellate authority

e: No appeal lies under the D and A Rules against an order imposing a penalty passed by the President himself.

q: A disciplinary authority subordinate to the authority which appointed a railway servant proposes to dismiss him from service. Under Article 311(1) of the Constitution, such an order of dismissal:

options.A: Can be passed by any authority senior to the railway servant
options.B: Can be passed by the subordinate authority with the approval of the Railway Board
options.C: Can be passed by the subordinate authority if the charges are grave
options.D: Cannot be passed by an authority subordinate to the authority by which he was appointed

e: Article 311(1) provides that no person shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he was appointed.

q: In a major penalty inquiry, the charged railway servant asks to see the documents which have been listed in the memorandum of charges as relied upon against him. The correct position is that he is entitled to:

options.A: Inspect, and take extracts from, the documents and records relied upon against him, as mentioned in the charge memorandum
options.B: Inspect the documents only after the inquiry is concluded
options.C: Receive only a summary of the documents, and not inspect the originals
options.D: Inspect the documents only through a legal practitioner engaged by him

e: In a major penalty inquiry the charged servant is entitled to inspect and take extracts from the listed documents relied upon in the charge memorandum.

q: A railway servant is selected for promotion to a higher post but refuses to accept the promotion. The consequence for him is that he is debarred from being considered for promotion for a period of:

options.A: Six months from the date of his refusal
options.B: Two years from the date of his refusal
options.C: One year from the date of his refusal
options.D: Three years from the date of his refusal

e: A servant who refuses promotion on his turn is debarred from consideration for promotion for one year from the date of refusal.

q: The child of a railway servant, drawing Children Education Allowance, resides in the hostel of a recognised school away from the station of posting of the railway servant. Hostel subsidy is reimbursed at the rate of Rs 8,437.50 per month per child. The total hostel subsidy admissible for a full period of twelve months is:
e: Hostel subsidy for twelve months is Rs 8,437.50 x 12 = Rs 1,01,250 per child.

q: A candidate belonging to the Other Backward Classes applies for direct recruitment to a post on the Railways and claims relaxation in the upper age limit. The relaxation admissible to him is:

options.A: 5 years
options.B: 10 years
options.C: No relaxation is admissible to this category
options.D: 3 years

e: Other Backward Classes candidates get relaxation of three years in the upper age limit for direct recruitment to Central Government and Railway posts.

q: The services of a temporary railway servant, who is not a quasi-permanent servant, are to be terminated by the competent authority otherwise than as a measure of penalty. Such termination can ordinarily be effected by:

options.A: Giving him one month's notice in writing, or pay in lieu of such notice
options.B: Giving him three months' notice in writing in all cases
options.C: Giving him six months' notice in writing in all cases
options.D: Holding a full departmental inquiry before terminating his services

e: A temporary servant who is not quasi-permanent can be terminated, otherwise than by way of penalty, by one month notice in writing or pay in lieu thereof.

q: A railway servant dies in service without having made any nomination for gratuity, and no valid nomination subsists in his case. The gratuity payable on his death is paid:

options.A: Only to his widow or widower, to the exclusion of all other members of the family
options.B: Only to his eldest surviving son
options.C: To the members of his family in equal shares
options.D: To the Railways, as it lapses in the absence of a nomination

e: Where no nomination for gratuity subsists, death gratuity is paid to the members of the family in equal shares under the Pension Rules.

q: A railway servant dies in service after completing only seven months of continuous service. He had been medically examined and declared fit for railway service at the time of his appointment. In regard to family pension for his family, the correct position is that:

options.A: Family pension is not admissible, as he had not completed ten years of service
options.B: Family pension is admissible, as he had been medically examined and declared fit at the time of his appointment, even though he had completed less than one year of service
options.C: Family pension is admissible only at half the normal rate in such a case
options.D: Only death gratuity is admissible, and family pension can never be paid in such a case

e: Family pension is admissible even if the servant died before completing one year of service, if he had been medically examined and declared fit at the time of appointment.

q: Over different spells of Leave Travel Concession during his service, a railway servant has already encashed a total of 60 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. He now avails a fresh Leave Travel Concession and applies for encashment of 10 more days of Leave on Average Pay. His application is liable to be:

options.A: Granted, as 10 days can be encashed with every Leave Travel Concession without any overall limit
options.B: Granted, as the overall limit for such encashment in service is 100 days
options.C: Granted, as the overall limit for such encashment in service is 90 days
options.D: Refused, as the total encashment of Leave on Average Pay availed with Leave Travel Concession during the entire service cannot exceed 60 days

e: Encashment of Leave on Average Pay with Leave Travel Concession is limited to 10 days at a time and 60 days in the entire service, so beyond 60 days it must be refused.

q: A railway pensioner who retired on superannuation applies for commutation of a portion of his pension fourteen months after the date of his retirement. Before commutation is allowed in his case, he is required to:

options.A: Undergo a medical examination, as he has applied more than one year after his retirement
options.B: Do nothing further, as no medical examination is ever required on superannuation
options.C: Apply afresh for pension through his last office
options.D: Obtain a certificate from the pension disbursing bank about his health

e: Commutation without medical examination is allowed only within one year of retirement; after one year, as here at fourteen months, medical examination is required.

q: A probationer completes his period of probation satisfactorily, but no specific order of his confirmation is issued by the competent authority. He claims that he stands automatically confirmed on the expiry of the probation period. His claim is:

options.A: Correct, as confirmation follows automatically on completion of probation
options.B: Correct, if his Annual Performance Appraisal Reports for the probation period are above average
options.C: Not correct, as there is no deemed confirmation and confirmation requires a specific order of the competent authority
options.D: Correct, if no adverse entry was made in his service record during probation

e: Confirmation is not automatic on completion of probation; there is no deemed confirmation and a specific order of the competent authority is required.

q: Following a retrospective order of promotion, arrears of pay and allowances become due to a railway servant for a past period. These arrears are drawn:

options.A: Through the regular pay bill of the current month along with the normal salary
options.B: Through a supplementary bill, after the prescribed internal check of the arrears claim
options.C: Through a contingent bill of the office
options.D: Only at the time of his retirement, along with his settlement dues

e: Arrears due on a retrospective promotion order are drawn through a supplementary bill after the prescribed internal check, not in the regular pay bill.

q: A railway servant is granted study leave for an approved course of study. The leave salary admissible to him during the period of study leave is equal to:

options.A: Nil, as study leave is treated as leave without pay
options.B: Half of the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay
options.C: The subsistence allowance admissible to a railway servant under suspension
options.D: The leave salary which would have been admissible to him on Leave on Average Pay, together with the allowances admissible therewith

e: Study leave salary equals the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay, together with the allowances admissible therewith.

q: A railway servant lends money, at interest, to a contractor firm which has regular official dealings with his office, without obtaining any sanction. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, his action is:

options.A: Impermissible, as a railway servant shall not lend money to, or borrow money from, or otherwise place himself under a pecuniary obligation to, a person or firm having official dealings with him, without the previous sanction of the competent authority
options.B: Permissible, as the transaction is a purely private matter
options.C: Permissible, provided the rate of interest charged is the market rate
options.D: Permissible, provided he reports the transaction in his annual property return

e: Rule 18 of the Conduct Rules bars lending to, borrowing from, or placing oneself under pecuniary obligation to a person or firm having official dealings, without previous sanction.

q: A railway servant accepts a valuable gift from a contractor who has official dealings with his office, without obtaining any sanction and without reporting the matter. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, his conduct is:

options.A: Permissible, as gifts on ceremonial occasions are always allowed
options.B: Permissible, if the value of the gift is below the limit prescribed for reporting of gifts from relatives
options.C: Impermissible, as a railway servant shall not accept any gift from a person or firm having official dealings with him except with the sanction of the competent authority, in accordance with the rules
options.D: Impermissible only if the gift is accepted during his office hours

e: A railway servant shall not accept any gift from a person or firm having official dealings with him except with the sanction of the competent authority under the Conduct Rules.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System wishes to withdraw the whole of the amount lying in his Tier-II account while still in service, for a family purpose. In regard to the Tier-II account, the correct position is that:

options.A: No withdrawal is permitted from it before he attains the age of 60 years
options.B: It is a voluntary savings account, from which he can withdraw his savings at any time
options.C: Withdrawal from it is permitted only for purchase of an annuity on retirement
options.D: It is the account in which only the Government's co-contribution is accumulated

e: NPS Tier-II is a voluntary savings account with no lock-in like Tier-I, so the subscriber can withdraw the whole amount at any time while in service.

q: A railway pensioner surrenders Rs 1,500 per month of his pension for commutation. The commutation value for his age on the next birthday, 64 years, is 8.194 for each rupee of monthly pension surrendered. The lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Commuted value is monthly pension surrendered x factor x 12: Rs 1,500 x 8.194 x 12 = Rs 1,47,492.

q: A railway servant is convicted on a criminal charge by a court of law and a penalty is proposed to be imposed on him on the ground of the conduct which led to his conviction. In regard to the procedure for imposing that penalty, the correct position under Article 311(2) of the Constitution is that:

options.A: The penalty can be imposed without holding a departmental inquiry, on the ground of the conduct which led to his conviction
options.B: A full departmental inquiry must invariably be held before any penalty is imposed
options.C: The penalty can be imposed only after consulting the Union Public Service Commission in every case
options.D: No penalty can ever be imposed on a convicted railway servant

e: The second proviso to Article 311(2) permits imposing a penalty without inquiry on the ground of conduct which has led to conviction on a criminal charge.

q: The disciplinary authority records, in writing, its reasons for being satisfied that it is not reasonably practicable to hold a departmental inquiry against a railway servant in the prescribed manner. In such a case, under Article 311(2) of the Constitution:

options.A: The inquiry must still be held, but in camera
options.B: The penalty can be imposed on the railway servant dispensing with the holding of the inquiry
options.C: The railway servant must be retired compulsorily in all such cases
options.D: The case must be transferred to a court of law for trial

e: The third proviso to Article 311(2) permits dispensing with inquiry where the authority is satisfied, for reasons recorded in writing, that it is not reasonably practicable to hold it.

q: An appeal preferred by a railway servant against an order imposing a penalty on him is couched in disrespectful and improper language and merely repeats the arguments already rejected in an earlier appeal on the same matter. In regard to such an appeal, the correct position under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is that:

options.A: The appeal must invariably be forwarded to the appellate authority, whatever its contents
options.B: The appeal gives the railway servant a right to a personal hearing in all cases
options.C: The appeal is liable to be withheld by the authority to whom it is submitted, for the reasons recorded by it
options.D: The appeal automatically suspends the operation of the penalty order

e: An appeal that is couched in disrespectful language or repeats a previously decided appeal is liable to be withheld by the authority to whom it is submitted, for reasons recorded.

q: A railway servant is convicted by a court of law on a criminal charge and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment exceeding 48 hours. In regard to his suspension from duty, the correct position is that he is:

options.A: Entitled to continue in duty until his appeal against the conviction is decided
options.B: Treated as having been granted leave for the period of imprisonment
options.C: Required to apply for suspension in the prescribed form
options.D: Deemed to have been placed under suspension with effect from the date of his conviction

e: A servant convicted and sentenced to imprisonment exceeding 48 hours is deemed to have been placed under suspension from the date of conviction under the D and A Rules.

q: A railway servant has already earned two regular promotions during his service and completes 30 years of regular service without earning any further promotion. In regard to financial upgradations admissible to him under the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme, the correct position is that:

options.A: Only one financial upgradation is admissible to him under the Scheme, the two regular promotions being offset against the upgradations
options.B: Three financial upgradations are admissible to him, in addition to the two regular promotions
options.C: No financial upgradation is admissible to him, as he has already earned two promotions
options.D: Financial upgradations are admissible to him at 10, 20 and 30 years, ignoring the regular promotions altogether

e: MACP allows three financial upgradations in all at 10, 20 and 30 years, counting regular promotions; two promotions plus 30 years service therefore leave only one upgradation.

q: A railway servant who joined railway service on or after 01.01.2004 and is covered under the National Pension System claims subscription to the General Provident Fund. In regard to his claim, the correct position is that:

options.A: He can subscribe to the General Provident Fund in addition to his pension account, without any restriction
options.B: Subscription to the General Provident Fund is not admissible to him, as he is governed by the National Pension System and not by the old pension scheme
options.C: He can subscribe to the General Provident Fund only after completing ten years of service
options.D: He can subscribe to the General Provident Fund only with the special sanction of the Railway Board

e: Servants joining on or after 01.01.2004 are governed by NPS and the old pension scheme, including General Provident Fund subscription, does not apply to them.

q: A retired railway servant is re-employed under the Government after his retirement and his pay on re-employment is fixed after taking his pension into account. In regard to Dearness Relief on his pension during the period of such re-employment, the correct position is that:

options.A: Dearness Relief is admissible to him at double the normal rate during re-employment
options.B: Dearness Relief is admissible to him in full, in addition to his re-employment pay
options.C: Dearness Relief on his pension is not admissible to him during the period of such re-employment
options.D: His pension itself is stopped altogether during the period of re-employment

e: Dearness Relief on pension is not admissible during re-employment where pay is fixed after taking pension into account, though the pension itself continues.

q: The monthly wages of a railway servant employed in a workshop are Rs 40,000. Under Section 7(3) of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the total amount of deductions that can be made from his wages in a wage period, not being deductions wholly of the kind prescribed for payments to co-operative societies, shall not exceed:
e: Section 7(3) of the Payment of Wages Act caps total deductions at 50 per cent of wages, except cooperative society deductions; 50 per cent of Rs 40,000 = Rs 20,000.

q: A railway servant on tour is provided with free boarding and free lodging for a day, the admissible rate of Daily Allowance for the station being Rs 800 per day. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day, at 25 per cent of the admissible rate where both free boarding and free lodging are provided, will be:

options.A: Rs 200
options.B: Rs 400
options.C: Rs 600
options.D: Rs 800

e: Where both free boarding and free lodging are provided on tour, Daily Allowance is 25 per cent of the rate; 25 per cent of Rs 800 = Rs 200.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 1,00,000 per month is sent on deputation to another organisation at the same station. Deputation (Duty) Allowance for deputation within the same station is payable at 5 per cent of basic pay, subject to a maximum ceiling of Rs 4,500 per month. The allowance admissible to him per month will be:
e: Deputation within the same station is 5 per cent of basic pay capped at Rs 4,500; 5 per cent of Rs 1,00,000 is Rs 5,000, so only Rs 4,500 is admissible.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System has Rs 1,60,000 standing as his own contribution in his Tier-I account and seeks the maximum permissible partial withdrawal from that account for a prescribed purpose. Partial withdrawal being permissible up to 25 per cent of the subscriber's own contribution, the maximum amount he can withdraw will be:
e: NPS partial withdrawal is limited to 25 per cent of the subscriber own contribution; 25 per cent of Rs 1,60,000 = Rs 40,000.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 6 years of qualifying service, that is, 12 completed six-monthly periods, and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 50,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity is half a month emoluments per completed six-monthly period: Rs 25,000 x 12 periods = Rs 3,00,000, payable when service is below pensionable qualifying service.

q: Children Education Allowance is reimbursed at Rs 2,812.50 per month per child, and in respect of a Divyangjan child it is reimbursed at double the normal rate (Rs 5,625 per month). The total amount admissible to a railway servant in a full year in respect of one such Divyangjan child will be:
e: For a Divyangjan child, Children Education Allowance is double the normal rate, Rs 5,625 per month, so for a year it is Rs 5,625 x 12 = Rs 67,500.

q: In a direct recruitment exercise on the Railways, 250 posts in a category are to be filled. Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities being admissible at 4 per cent of the vacancies, the number of posts reserved for such persons in that recruitment will be:

options.A: 25 posts
options.B: 10 posts
options.C: 5 posts
options.D: 4 posts

e: Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities is 4 per cent of vacancies; 4 per cent of 250 posts = 10 posts.

q: A candidate belonging to the persons with benchmark disabilities category applies for direct recruitment to a post on the Railways and claims relaxation in the upper age limit prescribed for the post. The relaxation in the upper age limit admissible to such a candidate is:

options.A: 3 years
options.B: 5 years
options.C: 10 years
options.D: 15 years

e: Persons with benchmark disabilities get relaxation of 10 years in the upper age limit for direct recruitment.

q: A group of railway servants in an office resorts to a strike in support of their service demands. Under Rule 7 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in regard to such action by railway servants, the correct position is that no railway servant shall:

options.A: Submit any representation in respect of his service conditions
options.B: Join a recognised trade union of railway servants
options.C: Apply for leave in accordance with the leave rules
options.D: Resort to, or in any way abet, any form of strike or coercion or physical duress in connection with any matter pertaining to his service or the service of any other railway servant

e: Rule 7 of the Conduct Rules provides that no railway servant shall resort to or abet any form of strike, coercion or physical duress in connection with service matters.

q: A railway servant wishes to permit his spouse, who is dependent on him, to accept regular employment in a private firm which has official dealings with the office in which he is posted. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in regard to such employment, the correct position is that:

options.A: It can be accepted only with the previous sanction of the prescribed authority, obtained through the railway servant
options.B: No sanction or intimation of any kind is required for the employment of a spouse
options.C: It can be accepted freely, provided the railway servant himself has no dealing with the firm
options.D: It can be accepted only after the railway servant retires from service

e: Employment of a dependent spouse in a firm having official dealings with the servant office requires previous sanction of the prescribed authority, sought through the railway servant.

q: The classification of a category of railway staff under the Hours of Employment Regulations into classes such as 'Intensive', 'Continuous' and 'Essentially Intermittent' is determined on the basis of:

options.A: The length of service rendered by the staff in the category
options.B: A job analysis of the duties of the category, examining the nature and continuity of the work performed
options.C: The pay level held by the staff in the category
options.D: The choice exercised by the staff of the category themselves

e: Classification under the Hours of Employment Regulations as Intensive, Continuous or Essentially Intermittent is based on job analysis of the nature and continuity of the work.

q: An adult worker employed in a railway workshop, governed by the Factories Act, 1948, has already worked continuously for five hours at a stretch on a day. Under Section 55 of that Act, in regard to his further work on that day, the correct position is that he shall not be required or allowed to work further unless he has had:

options.A: An interval for rest of at least fifteen minutes
options.B: Permission of the Inspector of Factories in writing
options.C: An interval for rest of at least half an hour
options.D: A compensatory holiday in the following week

e: Section 55 of the Factories Act requires an interval of rest of at least half an hour after five hours of continuous work before the worker works further.

q: An adult worker is employed in a railway workshop governed by the Factories Act, 1948. In regard to the spread-over of his hours of work on any day, inclusive of his intervals for rest, the correct position under that Act is that the spread-over shall not exceed:

options.A: 9 hours in a day
options.B: 12 hours in a day
options.C: 8 hours in a day
options.D: Ten and a half hours in a day

e: Section 56 of the Factories Act limits the spread-over of hours of work, including rest intervals, to ten and a half hours in a day.

q: A temporary railway servant, who does not hold a permanent post, applies for Leave Not Due on medical certificate, no Leave on Half Average Pay being at his credit. In regard to the admissibility of Leave Not Due in his case, the correct position is that:

options.A: Leave Not Due is ordinarily admissible only to a permanent railway servant, and is not ordinarily admissible to a temporary railway servant
options.B: Leave Not Due is admissible to temporary and permanent railway servants on identical terms in all cases
options.C: Leave Not Due is admissible only to temporary railway servants, and not to permanent railway servants
options.D: Leave Not Due can be granted to a temporary railway servant without any limit

e: Leave Not Due is ordinarily admissible only to a permanent railway servant on medical certificate; it is not ordinarily admissible to a temporary servant not holding a permanent post.

q: A railway servant who is ordered to proceed on tour on duty requires funds to meet his travelling expenses during the tour. In regard to such expenses, the facility admissible to him under the Travelling Allowance rules is that:

options.A: He must meet the entire expenditure from his own pocket and claim reimbursement afterwards in all cases
options.B: He may draw an advance of Travelling Allowance for the tour, which is adjusted against his Travelling Allowance claim for the journey
options.C: He may draw his full salary for the following month in advance for the tour
options.D: He may draw an advance only after the tour has been completed

e: Travelling Allowance rules permit drawal of an advance of Travelling Allowance for a tour, to be adjusted against the TA claim for that journey.

q: A claim for arrears of pay of a railway servant, arising from a retrospective order, is not preferred within three years of the date on which the arrears became due. In regard to such a claim, the correct position is that:

options.A: The claim can never be paid under any circumstances
options.B: The claim must be paid immediately, without any examination
options.C: The claim is treated as time-barred and can be paid only after the prescribed investigation of the claim and with the sanction of the competent authority
options.D: The claim is payable only out of the Staff Benefit Fund

e: A time-barred arrears claim not preferred within three years can be paid only after the prescribed investigation and with the sanction of the competent authority.

q: A railway pensioner is convicted by a court of a serious crime after his retirement. In regard to his pension in such a case, the correct position under the pension rules is that:

options.A: His pension can never be touched, whatever the offence committed by him
options.B: His pension is automatically enhanced on his release from imprisonment
options.C: Only his Dearness Relief can be stopped, and his pension itself is fully protected
options.D: His pension, or a part of it, may be withheld or withdrawn by the competent authority, as future good conduct is an implied condition of the grant of pension

e: Future good conduct is an implied condition of pension; on conviction for a serious crime the competent authority may withhold or withdraw pension in whole or part.

q: A railway servant makes a nomination in favour of two members of his family for the amount standing at his credit in the General Provident Fund. In regard to such a nomination, the correct position is that:

options.A: The nomination must specify the share of the amount payable to each nominee, so that the amount is distributed in those shares on his death
options.B: The amount is always divided equally among the nominees, whatever the nomination may say
options.C: A nomination can be made in favour of only one person in all cases
options.D: The shares of the nominees are decided by the Accounts Office after the death of the subscriber

e: A GPF nomination in favour of more than one person must specify the share payable to each nominee, and payment on death is made in those specified shares.

q: An applicant under the Right to Information Act, 2005 seeks information a part of which is exempt from disclosure, the remaining part being severable and not containing any exempt information. Under Section 10 of that Act, in regard to such a request, the correct position is that:

options.A: The entire request must be rejected because a part of the information is exempt
options.B: Access may be provided to that part of the record which is not exempt and which can reasonably be severed from the exempt part
options.C: The exempt part must also be disclosed, as severance is not permissible
options.D: The application must be transferred to the Central Information Commission for a decision

e: Section 10 of the RTI Act permits severance: access may be given to the non-exempt part of a record that can reasonably be severed from the exempt part.

q: A candidate is selected for appointment to a post on the Railways. In regard to his medical fitness for appointment, the correct position is that:

options.A: No medical examination of any kind is required before appointment to a railway post
options.B: Medical examination is required only for posts in the running categories
options.C: He shall not be appointed to the post unless he has been declared medically fit for the post by the competent medical authority, as prescribed for the category
options.D: A medical certificate from any private practitioner is sufficient in all cases for appointment

e: No candidate shall be appointed to a railway post unless he has been declared medically fit for that post by the competent medical authority prescribed for the category.

q: The son of a railway servant who retires on superannuation in the normal course claims appointment on compassionate grounds as a matter of right on his father's retirement. In regard to such a claim, the correct position is that:

options.A: Appointment on compassionate grounds is a matter of right for the wards of all retired railway servants
options.B: Such appointment is admissible to the ward of every retiring railway servant, subject only to medical fitness
options.C: Such appointment can be claimed by the ward after any number of years from the retirement
options.D: Appointment on compassionate grounds is not a matter of right; it is admissible only in the prescribed cases, such as death in harness or retirement on medical grounds, where the family is in indigent circumstances and a vacancy is available within the prescribed quota

e: Compassionate appointment is not a matter of right; it is allowed only in prescribed cases like death in harness or medical retirement, where the family is indigent and a vacancy exists within the quota.

q: A railway servant is undergoing the currency of a penalty of withholding of increments imposed on him, and his case comes up for consideration for promotion to a higher post during that period. In regard to his promotion during the currency of the penalty, the correct position is that:

options.A: He is not eligible for promotion during the currency of the penalty and can be considered only after the penalty has expired
options.B: The penalty has no bearing at all on his eligibility for promotion
options.C: He must be promoted with retrospective effect from the date his junior is promoted
options.D: He is permanently debarred from promotion on account of the penalty

e: A servant is not eligible for promotion during the currency of a penalty of withholding of increments and can be considered only after the penalty expires.

q: A gazetted railway officer is required to attend office and perform duty on a national holiday and claims National Holiday Allowance for the duty so performed. In regard to his claim, the correct position is that:

options.A: National Holiday Allowance is admissible to gazetted and non-gazetted staff alike
options.B: National Holiday Allowance is admissible only to eligible non-gazetted railway servants who are required to work on a national holiday, and not to gazetted officers
options.C: National Holiday Allowance is admissible to gazetted officers at double the rate admissible to other staff
options.D: National Holiday Allowance has been extended to all railway servants irrespective of the nature of duty

e: National Holiday Allowance is admissible only to eligible non-gazetted servants required to work on a national holiday, not to gazetted officers.

q: A retired railway servant continues to occupy the railway quarter allotted to him long after the expiry of the period of retention permissible to him after retirement, without any authority. In regard to such unauthorised occupation of the quarter, the correct position is that:

options.A: No charge of any kind can be recovered from him for the period of unauthorised occupation
options.B: He acquires a right to retain the quarter permanently on payment of normal licence fee
options.C: He is liable to pay damage rent for the period of unauthorised occupation and to eviction proceedings under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act
options.D: Only his complimentary passes can be withheld for the unauthorised occupation

e: Unauthorised occupation of a railway quarter after the permitted retention period makes the retired servant liable to damage rent and eviction under the Public Premises Act.

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme seeks voluntary retirement after completing the prescribed qualifying service. In regard to the assured payout admissible to him in such a case, the correct position under the Scheme is that:

options.A: The assured payout commences immediately from the day following his voluntary retirement in all cases
options.B: No assured payout of any kind is admissible on voluntary retirement under the Scheme
options.C: He is paid only his own contribution, and the Government contribution is forfeited
options.D: The assured payout becomes payable to him only from the date on which he would have superannuated in the normal course, and not from the date of his voluntary retirement

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, on voluntary retirement the assured payout becomes payable only from the date the servant would have superannuated, not from the voluntary retirement date.

q: An office on the Railways proposes to prescribe a wage period of two months for the payment of wages to its staff, for administrative convenience. Under Section 4 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, in regard to such a proposal, the correct position is that:

options.A: No wage period so fixed shall exceed one month
options.B: A wage period of up to three months is permissible with the approval of the Head of Office
options.C: There is no restriction of any kind on the length of a wage period
options.D: A wage period must be fixed at exactly one week in all cases

e: Section 4 of the Payment of Wages Act provides that no wage period fixed by the employer shall exceed one month.

q: A railway servant is offered a foreign award, carrying a monetary benefit, by a foreign organisation in recognition of work done by him in his official capacity, and he wishes to accept it. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in regard to such acceptance, the correct position is that:

options.A: He can accept the award freely, as it is a recognition of his personal merit
options.B: He shall not accept the award without the sanction of the President of India
options.C: He can accept the award with the verbal permission of his immediate superior
options.D: He can accept the award after merely intimating his office about it

e: A foreign award carrying monetary benefit for official work cannot be accepted by a railway servant without the sanction of the President of India under the Conduct Rules.

q: A railway servant becomes a member of an association whose objects are prejudicial to the sovereignty and integrity of India and to public order. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in regard to a railway servant joining such an association, the correct position is that:

options.A: A railway servant may join any association of his choice without any restriction
options.B: Only gazetted railway servants are prohibited from joining such associations
options.C: No railway servant shall join, or continue to be a member of, any such association whose objects or activities are prejudicial to the sovereignty and integrity of India, public order or morality
options.D: Membership of such an association is permissible with the permission of the trade union of his category

e: The Conduct Rules bar a railway servant from joining or continuing in any association whose objects or activities are prejudicial to sovereignty and integrity of India, public order or morality.

q: A non-gazetted railway servant is posted to a hill station and applies for Warm Clothing Advance for the purchase of warm clothing. In regard to that advance under the present (7th CPC) dispensation, the correct position is that:

options.A: An interest-bearing advance, recoverable with interest at the rate applicable to House Building Advance
options.B: A free grant which is never required to be recovered
options.C: Recoverable only from the gratuity payable to him at retirement
options.D: Warm Clothing Advance stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation and is no longer admissible

e: Warm Clothing Advance was among the advances abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation and is no longer admissible.

q: The pay of the staff of a railway office for a month is ordinarily disbursed on the last working day of the month, and the last day of the month happens to be a public holiday. In regard to the disbursement of pay in such a case, the correct position is that:

options.A: The pay for the month is disbursed on the preceding working day, as the last day of the month is a holiday
options.B: The pay is disbursed only in the following month, along with the next month's pay
options.C: The pay is disbursed on the holiday itself by keeping the cash office open
options.D: The pay of the month is forfeited if it is not drawn on the last day

e: Pay is normally disbursed on the last working day; if the last day of the month is a holiday, pay is disbursed on the preceding working day.

q: In a major penalty inquiry, the case on behalf of the disciplinary authority is presented by a Presenting Officer who is a legal practitioner, and the charged railway servant seeks to engage a legal practitioner as his defence assistant. In regard to such engagement, the correct position under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is that:

options.A: A legal practitioner can never be engaged in a departmental inquiry under any circumstances
options.B: The charged railway servant may be allowed to engage a legal practitioner as his defence assistant, with the permission of the competent authority, in such a case
options.C: A legal practitioner can be engaged only after the inquiry has been concluded
options.D: The charged railway servant must engage a legal practitioner compulsorily in every inquiry

e: Where the prosecution case is presented by a legal practitioner, the charged servant may, with permission of the competent authority, engage a legal practitioner as defence assistant.

q: A railway servant is permanently absorbed in a public sector undertaking, with the permission of the competent authority, and claims encashment of the Leave on Average Pay standing at his credit on the date of his absorption. In regard to such encashment, the correct position is that:

options.A: The leave at his credit lapses entirely on his absorption and no encashment is admissible
options.B: Encashment is admissible only if he returns to railway service thereafter
options.C: Cash equivalent of the Leave on Average Pay at his credit, subject to the prescribed ceiling, is admissible to him on his permanent absorption, as in the case of retirement
options.D: Encashment is admissible only after he attains the age of superannuation in the undertaking

e: On permanent absorption in a public sector undertaking, cash equivalent of Leave on Average Pay at credit, subject to the prescribed ceiling, is admissible as on retirement.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System changes his place of posting from one Railway to another and later takes up another appointment, and is concerned about the continuance of his pension account. In regard to the Permanent Retirement Account Number allotted to him, the correct position is that:

options.A: A fresh account number is allotted to him at every new place of posting
options.B: His account is closed on his transfer from one Railway to another
options.C: He must withdraw the entire amount in his account on every change of appointment
options.D: The same Permanent Retirement Account Number remains operative throughout, the account being portable across locations and employments

e: The Permanent Retirement Account Number under NPS is a single portable account that remains operative across transfers, locations and employments.
